data.why: MNIST (the default configured dataset) is pre-downloaded into the repo's data/ folder during install via torchvision, matching the app's default FL_BACKDOOR_DATA_DIR so no network is needed once the server runs; the interface has no file-upload workflow for experiment input data.

goals: run a baseline federated learning experiment with no attack and no defense to establish clean ACC
launch a BadNets backdoor attack experiment and observe attack success rate (ASR) rise while accuracy stays high
enable a defense (e.g. Krum aggregation plus clustering detection) against the same attack and compare ACC/ASR to the undefended run
compare multiple attack/defense combinations side by side using the summary and comparison plots (accuracy vs ASR, detection precision/recall)
inspect per-client anomaly scores and confusion matrices to judge whether a detector separates malicious from benign clients

review.summary: The goal is stated well and the configuration side is documented accurately with good evidence: trigger preview, layered defense selector, backups, raw editor. Every launch failed with HTTP 500, though, so the tree never reaches the platform's purpose of comparing ACC/ASR and detection quality across attack/defense runs, and its phases reflect a debugging session (second-host login, failure diagnosis, a survey catch-all) instead of the research workflow.
